title: Non-invasive control of gene editing in vivo by photoswitchable Cas12f and focused ultrasound.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the only public dataset: BioProject PRJNA1516203 (Stanford), described as 'Deep sequencing data supporting Figures 4e, 4h, 6E'. Downloaded and parsed the full SRA run table (30 KB CSV): exactly 56 runs, all AMPLICON PCR, all Mus musculus, 153 MB total, 9,262-143,928 read pairs each, Illumina iSeq 100. Read all 56 sample names, which encode the whole experiment: 2 target sites (LSL reporter, TTR gene), 3 Cas12f variants (CasMINI, eCas12f1, AsCas12f-HKRA), 4 conditions (unfused, dark, light, focused ultrasound), 2-4 mice per group. Also confirmed: no PMC full text, Europe PMC hasSuppl=N, 0 hits for the DOI or 'photoswitchable Cas12f' on Zenodo and Dryad, Cell's own abstract page returns HTTP 403, and Addgene holds 5 plasmids (physical reagents, not data).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the protein engineering campaign (how many photoswitchable Cas12f variants were built and screened, cell-culture editing percentages, light/dark fold-induction) comes from the abstract alone, because the full text and supplementary tables are behind Cell's paywall and were never deposited in PubMed Central.

a1_downloadable.note: The 56 raw fastq runs in PRJNA1516203 are public, but the processed editing-efficiency tables - the only model-ready form of the data - exist solely in the paywalled Cell supplement. No PubMed Central deposit (Europe PMC: isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N), nothing on Zenodo or Dryad, publisher page returns 403.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label (percent insertion/deletion editing at the target site) is not a column in any public file. It would have to be constructed from scratch by running amplicon-analysis software such as CRISPResso2 over 56 fastq files, then aggregating per mouse.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are known in principle: three named Cas12f protein variants and two target sites, with the actual plasmid sequences obtainable from Addgene (IDs 261716-261721). But they are 5 reagents to look up, not features in a table.

a4_units_stated.note: No data table exists to carry units. Editing efficiency would be a percentage computed by whichever amplicon pipeline we chose, so the units would be ours, not the authors' - and not comparable to their published figures.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified in the SRA run table: 56 amplicon samples forming roughly 20 experimental groups with 2-4 mice each. The checklist needs about 1,500 labelled rows, or 400 for pure classification. This is two orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem: 153 MB total, CPU-only amplicon analysis. Verified from the size_MB column of the run table.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare. The BioProject description names Figures 4e, 4h and 6E, consistent with 56 samples, but the paper's own numbers are unreadable behind the paywall.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance would be clean if the label existed: editing percentage from targeted amplicon sequencing of mouse genomic DNA, a direct physical measurement, not another model's output.

existing_models.name: DeepCas12a (deep learning model predicting AsCas12a guide-RNA cutting efficiency from sequence plus chromatin data)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search results report average precision 0.783 and area under the ROC curve 0.868; I did not retrieve the paper, so I cannot state the split.

existing_models.name: DeepCpf1 (convolutional network predicting Cas12a guide efficiency, the long-standing reference model in this area)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; known from secondary descriptions in search results only.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join helps: 56 mouse amplicon samples covering 2 target sites cannot be extended by any public resource into a trainable table, because the variation the paper studies (light versus dark activation of one engineered protein) exists nowhere else.

controls.positive_control: Would have been easy if data existed: the model must recover the known light-versus-dark difference in editing. With 2-4 mice per group this is a t-test, not a model.
controls.negative_control: Unfused (always-on) Cas12f samples are present and act as the upper bound; dark samples act as the lower bound.
controls.external_validation: None. No second lab has built photoswitchable Cas12f variants activated by focused ultrasound.

honest_claim_h3: No honest machine-learning claim is available: with 56 amplicon samples across ~20 groups, any model would be describing a 20-cell summary table that the paper already reports as bar charts.

plain_idea.one_liner: Considered using engineered protein sequence and light condition to predict how much gene editing happens in mouse tissue.
plain_idea.train_on: Would have trained on each combination of Cas12f variant, target site and activation condition. Verified count: 56 sequencing samples, about 20 distinct groups - far too few.
plain_idea.predict: Percent of DNA molecules edited at the target site, measured by sequencing a short amplified stretch of mouse genomic DNA (targeted amplicon sequencing). That percentage is not published in any open file.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gene-editing labs would value a model that predicts which engineered switchable nuclease works best in which tissue, but this paper's data is a proof-of-concept demonstration, not a screen, so nothing can be learned from it by modelling.

more_or_better_data.why: 56 amplicon samples over 2 target sites, verified in the SRA run table. Published guide-efficiency models such as DeepCpf1 and DeepCas12a were trained on tens of thousands of guides from pooled screens.

confidence_score.why: There are only 2-4 mice per group, enough to see that light beats dark but far too few to estimate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: Irrelevant here: the existing Cas12a models predict guide-sequence efficiency, a different task from light-gated activation, and this dataset varies only 2 guides so it cannot train or test a guide-efficiency model at all.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: no baseline model exists for light-gated editing, no shared evaluation split, and the 56 samples do not join to any public dataset measuring the same quantity.

ml_idea: None viable. The only conceivable task - predict light-gated editing efficiency from Cas12f variant identity, target site and activation mode - has 56 observations in roughly 20 experimental groups, so the paper's own bar charts already contain all the information a model could extract.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the verified SRA run table: 56 amplicon fastq pairs totalling 153 MB, each ~9k-144k read pairs, so a CRISPResso2-style run is minutes per sample on CPU. No cross-validation is meaningful at this sample size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the public samples. One query of the SRA run table for PRJNA1516203 returns 56 amplicon runs in ~20 groups, which kills the project in two minutes - and I ran it.

verdict_reason: 56 mouse amplicon samples, editing label only in the paywalled supplement, no public table.
